LESSON: SHORT FORMS • C-H

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: GRADE
Strand: English Braille
Topic 4.2: Short forms • C-H
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Short forms • C-H, part of English Braille in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: How do short forms help in writing faster?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. explore tactile Braille cards with short forms (C–H) by touch, pronounce the words aloud, and match them to printed flashcards with their meanings,

2. play a Braille short form memory game, flipping over Braille and print cards to find matching pairs of short forms and full words (e.g., “could” ↔ “c”),

3. compose short Braille sentences using C–H short forms on a slate and stylus or Braille machine, then swap with a peer for reading and correction,

4. use Braille story cards, to identify and underline all C–H short forms using tactile markers, then read the story aloud in pairs,

5. engage in a “short form speed-write” activity,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. explore tactile Braille cards with short forms (C–H) by touch, pronounce the words aloud, and match them to printed flashcards with their meanings,
2. play a Braille short form memory game, flipping over Braille and print cards to find matching pairs of short forms and full words (e.g., “could” ↔ “c”),
3. compose short Braille sentences using C–H short forms on a slate and stylus or Braille machine, then swap with a peer for reading and correction,
4. use Braille story cards, to identify and underline all C–H short forms using tactile markers, then read the story aloud in pairs,
5. engage in a “short form speed-write” activity,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Short forms • C-H together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to Learn: the learners develop strategies to apply short forms in new contexts.

● Communication and Collaboration: the learners engage in group writing and reading exercises.

Values

● Cooperation: the learner assists peers in mastering short forms through paired practice.

● Integrity: the learner uses short forms correctly and consistently.
